hens_rule_text: up to 6 female chickens as an accessory use in single-family residential districts (RE-1 lots follow livestock animal-unit rules instead)
permit_notes: A permit is required for the accessory structure (coop). No separate animal license is mentioned.
setback_notes: Coop must be in the rear yard and meet accessory structure rules in CZO 14-102.B.1-6; exact distances not confirmed.
coop_rules: Chickens must be housed in a fully enclosed accessory structure located in the rear yard.
zoning_notes: Only female chickens are allowed on single-family residential lots, so roosters are effectively limited to RE-1 (animal units by acreage) and A-1 (no livestock limit) districts. Slaughter is not permitted on residentially zoned property.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Chesapeake Zoning Administration: Chickens and Chicken Coops

research_notes: Read the official city zoning page directly, which quotes CZO 14-101.C.2.f. Coop setback distances in 14-102.B were not readable (Municode blocked), and rooster status is inferred from the female-only wording.
